GettingStartedwithEdgeAI.title: Getting Started with Edge AI
GettingStartedwithEdgeAI.description: Edge AI is about adding AI or ML models right on the edge on small constrained devices. Infineon & DEEPCRAFT help to simplify the process of adding intelligence to your products
GettingStartedwithEdgeAI.long_description:
Edge AI is the process of developing small and efficient machine learning models intended for running at the edge of the system close to the events happening. Typically you want to run these models locally, you need fast response times and they are intended to run in smaller devices. In Infineon we typically are talking about microcontrollers e.g. PSOC™, AURIX™, TRAVEO™ families.

The DEEPCRAFT™ AI Hub brings together tools, solutions, Accelerators, and pre-trained models for Infineon embedded platforms — so you can browse, compare, and deploy AI on PSOC™ and AURIX™ hardware from one place. Each entry includes metadata such as supported sensors, target devices, kits, and application domains. Use the Hub to find the right starting point for your project, then follow the linked resources to download software, flash firmware, or open a project in DEEPCRAFT™ Studio.

The Edge AI journey is split up into multiple steps:
* Data Collection: The DEEPCRAFT™ Studio helps you with data collection
* Model Development: You can use the DEEPCRAFT™ Studio to help you with training and the DEEPCRAFT™ Studio Accelerators to get started with an existing use-case and dataset we also may have other content under model development that is using python and other frameworks
* Model Deployment: after training/building a model you need to get it to a format to run on a microcontroller here you can use DEEPCRAFT™ Studio & DEEPCRAFT™ Model Converter. You can also find customer and open source models we have deployed on our hardware here on the AI Hub

Outside of this you have solutions, if you want a solution ready to integrate directly into your application without going the process of building and preparing a model.

DEEPCRAFTModelConverter.title: DEEPCRAFT™ Model Converter
DEEPCRAFTModelConverter.description: Converts, optimizes and validates AI models for Infineon MCUs
DEEPCRAFTModelConverter.long_description: The DEEPCRAFT™ Model Converter is a software application that supports the Bring Your Own Model concept (BYOM), which allows users to bring their own AI model and run it on edge devices. This application helps machine learning engineers work more efficiently, by streamlining the processes for running their models on their target hardware. Models are converted so they can run on the edge. Models are optimized, which means they will become highly compact and high-performance models, designed to run on Infineon MCUs. Models are validated with a dataset to check that the generated code matches the performance in the original models. Validation is done on the desktop, it has an easy-to-use Graphical User Interface (GUI) and runs on Windows, Linux and Mac. It also includes a Command Line Interface (CLI) to enable integration into Continuous Integration (CI)/Continuous Delivery (CD) pipelines and workflows.

Solutions.title: Solutions
Solutions.description: Production-ready DEEPCRAFT™ Ready Models and edge AI software solutions from Infineon — the fastest way to production in the Hub.
Solutions.long_description:
The Solutions section features fully developed models and applications you can download, evaluate on supported hardware, and integrate into your product—without training a model from scratch. Solutions skip the full model development cycle and give you field-proven models already optimized for Infineon MCUs. Each solution includes metadata for sensors, target devices, compatible kits, application domains, and performance metrics (memory usage, inference time, and power where available). Solutions are maintained by Infineon and are not open for community contribution.

On the cards you'll typically find information about the Edge AI solution, the performance and metrics for the solution and a link that takes you to the product pages and where you can get started with the evaluating the solution.

GenerativeAIon&fortheEdge.title: Generative AI on & for the Edge
GenerativeAIon&fortheEdge.description: Generative AI is taking off and in this article series we look at how you can leverage it for building Edge AI models and running on the edge
GenerativeAIon&fortheEdge.long_description:
This 3-part article series looks at how to leverage Generative AI for the edge and then how to run it on the edge. The first article highlights 4 different ways you can use generative AI to help you with developing better Edge AI models. Namely it looks at how you can use it to assist you in your development journey, you can use it to help you find relevant data in big datasets, you can let it synthesise and generate new data for you and you can use it to improve your model accuracy.

In the next parts we explore how you can take them from the cloud and run them in the Edge, the impact and how this is evolving with the current advancement in hardware and computation.

LLMs and Generative AI is making a big impact across different sectors and the Edge AI sector is no different.

TheFutureofAutonomousSystems:Unlockingth.title: The Future of Autonomous Systems: Unlocking the Potential of Physical AI and Edge AI
TheFutureofAutonomousSystems:Unlockingth.description: Physical AI is very related to Edge AI. Find out what Physical AI is and how DEEPCRAFT™ fits into this
TheFutureofAutonomousSystems:Unlockingth.long_description: As technology continues to advance at a rapid pace, we're witnessing the emergence of new and exciting fields that are transforming the way we interact with machines. One such area that's gaining significant attention is Physical AI, a field that focuses on creating artificial intelligence systems that can adapt to and interact with their physical environment in real-time. In this blog post, we'll delve into the world of Physical AI, its connections to Edge AI, and how Edge AI software is supporting the development of autonomous systems. To learn more click on the article below.
